name: @tellma/core
description: The Tellma app framework: the runtime a distribution's single-page app imports, split into entry points along its lazy-loading lines.

Re-baselined from 12.5 to 12.24 when the gate moved to the linked production measure (12.21 linked against 12.47 on the published bundle), keeping the same 0.03 of headroom. Raised from 12.24 to 16.59 for the client store and the tab bus: measured 12.21 before and 16.51 after on the linked measure (+4.30 KB, including the storage-fault fallback, the sweep result and the sweep-over-earlier-writes rule; 12.47 before and 16.82 after on the published-bundle measure), keeping the 0.08 of headroom it had on that measure, within the 9 KB share of spec 0025's primary services. The weight is TmClientStore (the mirror with its idle-rule views, readAll over partition ranges, put with the savedAt rule, patch in one transaction, the write guard, the three sweeps with their prefix messages, the re-read on another tab's commit and on a return from the back-forward cache, the boot step, the open with its 3 s timeout, memory fallback and versionchange close, and the boot record's read, patch and storage-event stream), TmTabBus over two BroadcastChannels (the queue until the slug is known, the per-user channel that follows the session, the back-forward-cache close and reopen, the envelope filter), TM_DOC_FORMATS and the browser seam. rxjs stays external, as Angular already ships it. Savings taken: one transaction helper serves every read, write and sweep; the mirror and the pending-write count are plain maps; the boot record reuses the boot script's parser and storage helpers. Raised from 16.59 to 20.28 for the cache refresher and the launch documents: measured 16.51 before and 20.19 after on the linked measure (+3.68 KB), keeping 0.09 of headroom; with the client store and the tab bus, spec 0025's primary services now weigh 7.98 KB of their 9 KB share. The weight is TmCacheRefresher (observe, refresh with its coalesced runs, the sync lock, the re-check inside it, the 2 s throttle and the one-transaction store of the answer, adopt with its preferences and locale patches, the cache.changed handler with its jitters, the membership-boundary timer with its backoff, the error routing and the sync telemetry), TmLaunchCache (the launch documents, the tenant entry with its cold sync, the lazily loaded entity lists with their stale and refused rules, and the user documents' background reads), TmLocks with its in-tab fallback, and the store's several-document write, its show-ahead and its re-read. Savings taken: put, patch and the several-document write share one write helper and one pending count; the refresher and the launch cache keep their state in private fields, which the minifier shortens; the four client tags are a list, not a map. Raised from 20.28 to 20.44 for the review fixes to the refresher and the store: measured 20.19 before and 20.35 after on the linked measure (+0.16 KB), keeping 0.09 of headroom; spec 0025's primary services now weigh 8.14 KB of their 9 KB share. The weight is a cold call's test of the launch documents themselves, a list's call that ends once a sync in flight reports the list's tag, the clamp on a sync stamp ahead of the clock, and an adoption kept shown over a sync's write. Savings taken: the shown updates live on the mirror entry, not in a map of their own (0.06 KB). Raised from 20.44 to 31 for the bootstrap, the derived routes, the URLs, the query codec and the route host: measured 20.36 before and 30.87 after on the linked measure (+10.51 KB), the ceiling being that measurement rounded up to the next 0.5 KB. The weight is TmUrls (the builders with the no-tenant rule, target, describe over the route table's order, preload with its once-per-chunk set, and the codec's parsers), the search query codec (the canonical printer, the lenient parser with its dropped-entry reports, the in/between escapes and the #d= base64url payload), the route table with its matchers, canMatch rules and section-aware leave check, the reuse strategy that creates every route anew on a change of tenant, TmRouteHost (the skeleton, the parallel chunk, Entities and cold-entry loads, the focus holds it gives back, the securable gate, the update check on a chunk failure, the page scope and the leave checks), the page skeleton, the four error views (offline, client-outdated, forbidden and not-found) and the not-found page, TmTitleStrategy, TmPageFocus with its in-place rule, the launch redirect with its page at /, the launch timer, TmApp with its navigation-failure view, the startup initializers with the Contracts chunk's load at idle, TmEntities, the interim platform text, TmUrlSerializer and bootstrapTellma. Savings taken: the shell stand-ins and the one placeholder page live in ./shell, loaded with import(). The not-found page, the launch page at / and the forbidden view stay here: moved into ./shell they took about 0.6 KB out of this measure, but ./shell loads with every first frame, so the first frame saved nothing, and they moved back (a chunk of their own, loaded only when they render, is left to the full re-split); the error view is one data-driven component; the six page-family hosts share one loader; the builders of the routed tenant and of forTenant are one class over a path prefix; the services keep their state in private fields, which the minifier shortens. The development error messages stay, since a developer acts on them. Split by spec, roughly: spec 0025's primary services 8.1 KB of their 9 KB share; TmEntities about 0.5 KB, which is spec 0029's share; spec 0024's own services the remaining 22.3 KB or so, against their 14 KB share in spec 0024. The primary's 50 KB total is not reached. Raised from 31 to 36 for localization, the strings, server text and the theme: measured 30.87 before and 35.61 after on the linked measure (+4.74 KB), the ceiling being that measurement rounded up to the next 0.5 KB. The weight is TmLocalization (every member of the language, the regional formats, the calendar and the zones as signals over the launch documents, the boot record and the client metadata; the load-then-apply switch with its linked language and calendar; the per-tenant overrides that stand until the stored preference moves; the document and Transloco wiring; the message resolver with its English fallback, development warning and bidi strip; the device-zone re-read and the four telemetry events), the resolution rules (the region, the canonical digits extension and the once-per-tag browser check with its two fallbacks), the coalesced locale write (600 ms, one in flight, reset members, adoption, the offline retry, the pagehide send and the tenant-change flush), TmServerText, the calendar-aware argument formatter, the string loader with its collision rule, the English platform table, the theme glue with theme-color, the provideTellma wiring of the library tokens and the request locale, and the twelve directional platform icons (about 0.3 KB of lucide data, within the 4 KB icon share). Savings taken: the development errors and warnings sit behind the build-time ngDevMode flag, which a production build folds away with their text (0.15 KB); the interim platform text is gone, its resolver being TmLocalization's; the route error views carry keys only, their English living once in the English table. Split by spec, roughly: spec 0025's primary services 8.1 KB of their 9 KB share; TmEntities about 0.5 KB, which is spec 0029's share; the platform icon data 0.3 KB of its 4 KB share; spec 0024's own services the remaining 26.7 KB or so, against their 14 KB share. The primary's 50 KB total is not reached. The figures that follow are on the published-bundle measure. Raised from 1.5 to 4.5 for the distribution API: measured 1.26 before and 4.32 after (+3.06 KB). The weight is the merge rule behind TM_APP_DECLARATIONS (about 2.4 KB: keys, overrides, coded-report patches, hide and the app-bar rules, each problem recorded with its facts), then tmFeature and the declaration functions, provideTellma, the metadata loaders and TM_CLIENT_METADATA. Savings taken: the merge keeps its state in private fields, which the minifier shortens (0.11 KB), and the config check, which the spec places in the primary, lives in the lazy ./config-check instead. The primary's ceiling keeps growing towards the sum of its shares as each owner lands. Raised from 4.5 to 6.5 for the session and launch: measured 4.32 before and 6.34 after (+2.02 KB). The weight is TmSession (the profile cookie decoder, check, signIn with the sign-in mark and step-up parameters, and the mark consumption that sweeps a previous user's drafts), the session guard and paths (the expiry's cookie delete, reload and sign-in loop guard), TmLaunch with its router subscription, tmSingleLiveTenant, and the shared web-storage and boot-record helpers; the boot script's own logic and page builder are not in the primary, since the script runs before the app and hands its result over on window.__tmBoot. Savings taken: the session's writable state lives in TmSessionPaths instead of a third injectable, and check() compares the decoder-built profiles as JSON instead of member by member (0.05 KB together); the sign-in error messages stay, since a developer acts on them. Raised from 6.5 to 12.5 for the HTTP layer: measured 6.34 before and 12.27 after (+5.93 KB), within the 14 KB share of this spec's own services. The weight is TmHttpApi (the call pipeline: tenant routing, the Contracts lookups, the gates, the watchdog, retries with abortable waits, the status table, the outdated-client verdict with the worker cap, download streaming, the XHR upload, keepalive sends and the blob fetcher), the wire helpers (problem, Retry-After, version tags, step-up, Content-Disposition, trace ids, SemVer precedence), TmApiError, the reachability probe and the browser and service seams. Savings taken: fetch, XHR and blob fetches share one judging path (response check, observers, status table, verdict) instead of one per transport; the retry table is data driven; the layer keeps its state in private fields, which the minifier shortens. The development error messages stay, since a developer acts on them.
budgetNotes../config-check: Kept at 4.5 when the gate moved to the linked production measure (4.28 linked against 4.28 on the published bundle). The figures that follow are on the published-bundle measure. Born at 4.28 KB measured: tmCheckAppConfig, its problem messages and the entity-declaration checks. Lazy: the build runs it in Node, and only a development app loads it at startup.
budgetNotes../shell: Born at 1.19 KB measured, with 0.09 of headroom: the stand-ins for the tenant shell, the tenant picker and the signed-out page, and the placeholder page the page families render until their entry points land. Measured 1.22 KB with the component map the primary loads the shell's components by (+0.03 KB), within the 1.28 ceiling. The primary loads it with import(); spec 0027's shell replaces the stand-ins and raises this ceiling.
budgetNotes../private: Kept at 0.5 when the gate moved to the linked production measure (0.02 linked against 0.02 on the published bundle). The figures that follow are on the published-bundle measure. Empty at birth: the slot for shared wiring between this package's own entry points.
budgetNotes._: Ceilings are ratchets. Any raise belongs here with its reason; a raise with no note is a bug.
